ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image one can see a regular heptagon, with a diagonal drawn inside from the topmost vertex to the lower slightly right vertex, dividing the figure into a left pentagon and a right quadrilateral. The right quadrilateral has, along the boundary in order, the topmost vertex, the upper-right vertex, the lower-right vertex, and the lower vertex marked with angle x; x is the included angle between this diagonal and the lower-right side. According to the method, label the right quadrilateral as A-B-C-D: A is the topmost vertex, B and C are two consecutive vertices on the right boundary, D is the lower vertex marked with angle x, and AD is the drawn diagonal. Therefore x = ∠ADC. Because the original figure is a regular heptagon, the seven vertices all lie on the same circumcircle, and the arcs corresponding to adjacent vertices are equal, each small arc being 360/7 degrees. Angle ∠ADC is an inscribed angle, and the arc it intercepts is the arc from A to C passing through B; this arc contains the two adjacent small arcs AB and BC, so the measure of arc AC is 2·360/7. An inscribed angle equals half of the intercepted arc, so x = (1/2)(2·360/7) = 360/7 degrees.

method.method_draft: Label the visible right-hand quadrilateral as A-B-C-D, where A is the top vertex, B and C are the two consecutive vertices on the right boundary, D is the bottom vertex where x is marked, and AD is the drawn diagonal. Since the text says the polygon is a regular heptagon, all seven vertices lie on a circle and consecutive arcs are equal. The angle x is the inscribed angle ∠ADC, whose intercepted arc from A to C passes through B and covers exactly two side-arcs of the heptagon. Each side-arc has measure 360/7 degrees, so the intercepted arc has measure 2·360/7. An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc, giving x = 360/7.

Consecutive vertices of a regular heptagon subtend central angles of 360/7.
